waypoints.name: SR-20 Hairpin / Pond Pullout (east of Washington Pass)
waypoints.directions: Park in the pullout on the north side of SR-20 at the hairpin curve, roughly 0.3 to 0.5 mile past the Washington Pass Overlook turnoff and a short distance east of Washington Pass. SR-20 is gated for the winter and typically doesn't reopen until mid-to-late April or early May, so this approach isn't accessible until the highway opens for the season.

waypoints.name: Base of east face
waypoints.directions: Walk back west along the SR-20 shoulder toward the pass to the small pond on the south side of the highway, skirt the pond's east end, and pick up the cairned boot path heading north into the timber. It climbs steeply through forest for 15-20 minutes before breaking out onto talus directly beneath the East Face; the cairns are genuinely hard to follow before dawn, and there is no water between the car and the wall.

waypoints.name: Liberty Bell Mountain summit
waypoints.directions: From the talus, pick the line by the huge roof above you — the Lithuanian Lip — with Liberty Crack the continuous crack passing to its right; do not scramble straight up the fall line beneath it, which lands parties on the neighbouring East Face routes. The standard entry traverses in from the left for roughly 40 feet on third- and fourth-class ledges to the ledges under the true first-pitch crack, and twelve pitches then lead to the bolted alcove near the summit shoulder.

waypoints.name: Nooksack Cirque Trailhead
waypoints.directions: The Nooksack Cirque trailhead for Trail #750 sits at the end of Nooksack Cirque Road (FS-34), about a mile up from Hannegan Pass Road (FS-32) off the Mount Baker Highway, at about 2,200 ft. Cars stop on the near side of Ruth Creek: there is no bridge at the trailhead, and the crossing is made on foot on a large logjam a little downstream, with the trail and its registry box picked up on the far bank. In early summer, in high water, or after rain that crossing can be unsafe and has turned parties around before they started. Beyond it the first two miles are old roadbed on foot through old growth to the original trailhead site, so plan to walk from where you park rather than drive any closer. If you are climbing the Price, note that the standard descent comes out at the Lake Ann trailhead, so leave a shuttle vehicle or a second car there.

waypoints.name: Lake Ann Trailhead
waypoints.directions: The trailhead is on the east side of the Mount Baker Highway (SR-542), about a mile below Artist Point, at roughly 4,770 feet.

waypoints.name: Park Butte / Schriebers Meadow
waypoints.directions: From Sedro-Woolley, drive SR 20 east 16 miles to milepost 82 and turn left (north) on Baker Lake Road (FS 11). After 12 miles turn left on FS 12 and drive 3.6 miles to the FS 13 junction; stay right on FS 13 (Sulphur Creek Road) for 5.3 miles to its end at the Park Butte / Schriebers Meadow trailhead, about 3,360 ft. From the parking area, pick up Park Butte Trail 603 and cross Sulphur Creek on a footbridge or log crossing near the start — this can become a genuine ford during peak snowmelt.

waypoints.name: Sandy Camp / Railroad Grade Camp
waypoints.directions: Take Park Butte Trail 603 across Sulphur Creek (a footbridge or logs, a ford at peak melt) and up through the meadow and forest switchbacks to Morovitz Meadow, the last running water. At the signed junction there go right on Railroad Grade Trail 603.2, up stone steps onto the moraine crest, and follow it with the Easton Glacier dropping away on your right to Sandy Camp, where the crest runs out near 5,900 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Baker Summit
waypoints.directions: Rope up at the glacier edge and climb roughly north toward Sherman Peak, keeping climber's right of the main crevasse bands. Near 9,400 to 9,700 ft at the rim of Sherman Crater, cross the rockfall-swept slope quickly and trend west across the saddle to the foot of the Roman Wall, climb its 35 to 45 degree snow staying right of the rocky rib, then cross the summit plateau to Grant Peak.

waypoints.name: Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead (Trail #677, FR-39)
waypoints.directions: From the Mount Baker Highway (SR 542), turn onto Glacier Creek Road (FS 39) and follow it to the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead for Trail #677, at roughly 3,700 ft. Check the road first: FS 39 has a history of washouts, and when it has been closed low, parties have had to add several miles of road on foot or bike to reach the sign-in kiosk. When it is drivable, parking is limited and fills at weekends, and costs $5 a day or $30 for an annual pass. No climbing or wilderness permit is needed; the climbing register is voluntary. Glacier is the nearest supplies at 12 miles, with fuel in Maple Falls at 20 miles.

waypoints.name: Hogsback Camp
waypoints.directions: Follow Trail 677 as it switchbacks through old growth and avalanche chutes, crossing Grouse, Kulshan and Heliotrope Creeks (cross early, before afternoon melt). At the signed fork at about 2 miles go right on the climbers' path up the crest of the Hogsback moraine to the camps near 6,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Colfax–Baker Saddle
waypoints.directions: Rope up where the moraine meets the Coleman Glacier and climb south, then southeast toward the Black Buttes, weaving through crevasses. Higher, the track swings east beneath Colfax Peak; cross under its icefall without stopping, keeping off the avalanche-prone Colfax flank, to the broad saddle between Colfax and the summit cone at about 9,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Mt. Baker summit (Grant Peak)
waypoints.directions: From the saddle turn east and climb about 300 ft up the pumice ridge on a boot path, then the steep snow of the Roman Wall to the right of its rock, roughly 9,300 to 10,400 ft. Where it eases onto the flat summit plateau, walk about ten minutes to Grant Peak; wand the top of the wall for the way back.

waypoints.name: Cascade Pass Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road to its end, about 22 to 23 miles from Marblemount, to the large parking lot at the Cascade Pass Trailhead at 3,600 feet. If you plan to stay overnight at Sahale Glacier Camp, note that the permit is quota-limited — get an early-access wilderness permit or a walk-up the day before at the Marblemount ranger station.

waypoints.name: Cascade Pass
waypoints.directions: Follow the Cascade Pass Trail from the parking lot as it switchbacks steadily up through old-growth forest, roughly 1,800 ft in the first 2 miles, then eases across subalpine meadows to Cascade Pass at about 3.7 miles.

waypoints.name: Sahale Glacier Camp
waypoints.directions: At Cascade Pass take the left (north) fork signed for Sahale Arm and switchback up the open ridge crest, passing above Doubtful Lake. The final stretch above the Arm is loose scree and talus on cairns with real exposure, ending at the rock-walled tent pads of Sahale Glacier Camp.

waypoints.name: Sahale Mountain summit
waypoints.directions: From camp, rope up and climb the Sahale Glacier to the southwest base of the summit pyramid. A short, exposed stretch of steep snow and class 3-4 rock leads to a ledge just below the top, finished by an awkward chimney-like move onto the summit block.

waypoints.name: South Climb / Cold Springs Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Trout Lake, drive north on Mt Adams Road to the FR 23 junction and bear right about a mile to the signed FR 80 turn for South Climb. Follow FR 80 for 3.7 miles to FR 8040, then FR 8040 for 8.1 miles to its end at the South Climb / Cold Springs trailhead; it is steep and narrow with sharp switchbacks, so no RVs or trailers. Self-issue a free wilderness permit at the trailhead, and buy the Cascade Volcano Pass online beforehand to go above 7,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Adams Summit
waypoints.directions: Follow South Climb Trail #183 up an old roadbed through the burn, across the Round the Mountain Trail and the PCT, and up Crescent Ridge beside the Crescent Glacier to the Lunch Counter, a rocky bench at about 9,250-9,400 ft. Climb the south-facing snowfield of the South Spur about 2,400 ft to Piker's Peak, the false summit, then drop to the saddle and climb the last 600 ft or so of the summit cone to the old lookout on top.

waypoints.name: Climbers Bivouac Trailhead
waypoints.note: Highest vehicle access on the south side via FR-90/FR-83/FR-81/Spur 830; Ptarmigan Trail #216A starts here, and a climbing permit is required above 4,800 ft.
waypoints.directions: From Cougar, follow FR-90, FR-83, FR-81 and Spur 830 to the Climbers Bivouac trailhead at 3,700 ft, the highest vehicle access on this side of the mountain. Ptarmigan Trail #216A starts from the parking area. A climbing permit is required year-round above 4,800 ft and is checked at or near the trailhead; permits sell on Recreation.gov and release on the 1st of the prior month. Climbers Bivouac and the summer route are typically open and snow-free from late June through October.

waypoints.name: Ptarmigan Trail / Loowit Trail junction
waypoints.note: Ptarmigan Trail #216A meets the Loowit Trail (#216) here after climbing 900 ft through second-growth forest; continue straight/south to keep ascending toward timberline.
waypoints.directions: From the parking area pick up the signed Ptarmigan Trail #216A and follow it through second-growth forest for a little over two miles, gaining roughly 1,000 ft at an easy grade to the point where the Loowit Trail cuts across. Keep going straight and uphill rather than turning onto the Loowit. This stretch holds the only shade and the only seasonal creeklets on the route, and nothing above is dependable, so most parties carry all their water from the car.

waypoints.name: Timberline / permit-zone boundary
waypoints.note: Trees give out and the route opens onto Monitor Ridge's lava flows; this is the start of the year-round permit zone above which every climber must carry a self-issued or reserved permit.
waypoints.directions: A few hundred yards further the trees thin out and the tread gives way to the open lava and pumice of the ridge itself. This is the 4,800 ft line above which every climber must be carrying a permit, so it is the last place to sort that out. Before committing to the slope, find the first of the wooden posts and confirm the line you will be following.

waypoints.name: End of wooden route-marker posts
waypoints.note: Large wooden posts mark the boulder-hop route up Monitor Ridge to about this elevation; above here the tread disappears and the line is unmarked loose rock, pumice, and ash.
waypoints.directions: Above timberline the route follows a widely spaced line of tall wooden posts up boulder ribs and blocky old lava for about 2,200 ft; the rock ribs travel far better than the ash gullies beside them. Losing the post line in fog or low cloud is the biggest route-finding problem on the climb and a small drift off it puts you on steep, loose, off-route ground, so sight the next post before leaving the last. The posts run out near a GPS monitoring station at about 7,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Upper pumice/ash slope
waypoints.note: Roughly the last 1,300-1,500 ft is loose sandy pumice with no fixed path - climbers describe it as a 'two steps forward, one step back' slog; in whiteout or descent this section is easy to lose the ascent line on.
waypoints.directions: Past the last post there is no marked line and no tread at all — the ridge turns to deep sandy pumice and ash where every step gives back part of itself. Work the firmer rock ribs wherever they exist instead of wallowing straight up the ash. Take note of landmarks before you start up: this is the stretch where descending parties most often drift into a neighbouring drainage.

waypoints.name: Crater rim cornice / unstable edge
waypoints.note: USFS has repeatedly warned climbers to stay at least 30 ft back from the visible rim year-round - overhanging snow cornices and rockfall have caused fatal collapses even in summer.
waypoints.directions: Grind up the last thousand feet of loose ash to where the angle relents at the crater rim. Early in the season the same ground may be continuous snow, in which case an axe and crampons replace the slog and the descent can often be glissaded. Stop short of the edge — the rim is undercut, wind-built cornices here have broken away, and the standing advice is to stay at least 30 ft back from the visible lip in any season.

waypoints.name: Mount St. Helens summit (crater rim high point)
waypoints.note: True summit is about a quarter mile west along the crescent crater rim from where Monitor Ridge tops out; on clear days it offers views into the 1980-eruption horseshoe crater and lava dome.
waypoints.directions: The high point is a short walk west along the crescent of the rim from where Monitor Ridge tops out. Stay on the outer side of the crest the whole way and keep the same distance off the lip; there is nothing gained by walking the edge for the view into the crater.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road east from Marblemount for about 20 miles to the Eldorado trailhead pullout, about 3 miles short of the road's end at Cascade Pass, roughly 2,100 feet; the first ten miles are paved and the rest is gravel and washboard. There's a pit toilet at the parking area. The road typically doesn't open until late May or June, depending on snowpack. Camping here needs a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit reserved in advance, but the permit itself must be picked up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center before you drive up.

waypoints.name: Eldorado / Inspiration Glacier camp
waypoints.directions: Walk about 90 ft back down the road and cross the Cascade River on the log, then go about 100 ft straight away from the river to the climbers' path. It climbs steeply through timber for about 1,500 ft to a boulder field; follow cairns up it, staying climber's right of Eldorado Creek, into Eldorado Creek Basin. Cross the ridge at about 6,100 ft into Roush Basin, take talus and slabs onto the Eldorado Glacier, rope up, and climb it to camp near 7,500 ft.

waypoints.name: Inspiration Glacier
waypoints.directions: Roped, cross the nearly flat Inspiration Glacier toward the obvious low gap near the east end of Eldorado's East Ridge. Take a bearing from camp, because the glacier is featureless in cloud. Pass north through the gap onto the glacier slopes north of the ridge.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Climb west up the glacier slopes north of the ridge, keeping the crest on your left and probing suspect snow bridges, to where the slope steepens below the knife-edge. Follow the narrow, often corniced snow crest to the small summit. An axe and crampons are essential, and many parties place pickets along the crest.
